reason: Mars 2's dramatic crash and forgotten ski rover are thoroughly documented across multiple independent sources.
story: In May 1971, the Soviet Union launched Mars 2, a 4.6-ton spacecraft carrying humanity's boldest interplanetary gamble: an orbiter, a lander, and a rover. Tucked inside the descent capsule was PrOP-M, a miniature robotic rover designed to waddle across the Martian soil on skis while connected to its mothership by a 50-foot umbilical cable—more than 25 years before NASA deployed Sojourner. But when Mars 2 arrived on November 27, 1971, Mars was shrouded in one of the most ferocious planet-wide dust storms ever recorded. The landing craft separated and slammed into the Martian atmosphere at six kilometers per second. Due to a steep angle of entry, the landing sequence failed, the parachute never deployed properly, and the probe smashed into the ground. Mars 2 became the first human-made object to touch Mars, leaving behind a Soviet emblem and an undeployed rover, while its orbiter survived to map the dust-veiled world.
angle: The very first human-made object to touch Mars carried a tiny rover that walked on skis—25 years before NASA landed one—but it was destroyed in a planet-wide dust storm.

claims.claim: Mars 2 was launched by the Soviet Union on May 19, 1971.
Mars 2 was launched using a heavy Proton rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome.
Mars 2 had a total launch mass of approximately 4,650 kilograms.
Mars 2 was an integrated spacecraft consisting of an orbiter and an attached descent lander.
The lander carried a miniature robotic rover named PrOP-M.
The PrOP-M rover was engineered to traverse the Martian surface on skis rather than wheels.
The PrOP-M rover was tethered to the lander by a 15-meter (roughly 50-foot) umbilical cable.
When Mars 2 arrived, Mars was engulfed in one of the largest planet-wide dust storms ever recorded.
The descent lander separated from the orbiter roughly 4.5 hours prior to reaching Mars.
The landing craft entered the Martian atmosphere at a velocity of approximately 6 kilometers per second.
On November 27, 1971, Mars 2 became the first human-made object to reach the surface of Mars.
The lander's descent sequence failed and it crashed into the Martian surface.
Because the lander was destroyed upon impact, the PrOP-M rover was never deployed.
The lander carried a commemorative pennant bearing the State Emblem of the Soviet Union.
The Mars 2 orbiter entered an orbit around Mars with an 18-hour orbital period.
The Mars 2 orbiter completed 362 orbits around the planet.
Together, the Mars 2 and Mars 3 missions returned 60 photographs of Mars.
Twin spacecraft Mars 3 achieved a soft landing shortly after Mars 2, but its signal cut out after less than 20 seconds.

disputed: Parachute failure sequence: S1 and S7 state the parachute did not deploy at all, whereas S5 describes drogue and main chutes deploying but failing to brake adequately before a 500g impact. Scripts should attribute this simply as a failure of the landing and parachute system.

Life detection capability: S1 and S7 claim the lander carried a scoop to search for organic materials and signs of life, while S5 explicitly asserts no biological or life detection experiments were carried. Scripts should leave out any life detection claims.
Rover connection: S6 briefly calls PrOP-M an untethered rover in passing, but later affirms it was tethered by a 50-foot cable, matching S1, S2, and S7.

sources.title: On November 27, 1971 the Soviet Mars 2 became the first human-made object ever to reach the surface of Mars — but it arrived by crashing, its landing wrecked by one of the largest dust storms the planet has ever produced, carrying a tiny tethered rover on skis that would have driven on Mars 25 years before NASA's first, had it survived.

topic: Mars 2 (1971): the Soviet lander became the first human-made object to reach Mars on this day, crashing into the red planet after its parachute failed
